definitions.explanation: A small amount of an ingredient added to enhance flavor without being detectably present. The ingredient improves the dish subtly but isn't meant to be identified.

examples.japanese: このカレーの{隠|かく}し{味|あじ}は{蜂蜜|はちみつ}だ。
examples.english: The secret ingredient in this curry is honey.

examples.japanese: {隠|かく}し{味|あじ}に{味噌|みそ}を{少|すこ}し{加|くわ}える。
examples.english: Add a little miso as a secret ingredient.

examples.japanese: {隠|かく}し{味|あじ}が{効|き}いていて、{深|ふか}い{味|あじ}わいになっている。
examples.english: The secret ingredient works well, giving it a deep flavor.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{隠|かく}し{味|あじ}を{加|くわ}える (to add a secret ingredient)
・{隠|かく}し{味|あじ}に〜を{使|つか}う (to use ~ as a secret ingredient)
・{隠|かく}し{味|あじ}が{効|き}く (the secret ingredient works/takes effect)

COMMON {隠|かく}し{味|あじ} INGREDIENTS:
・{蜂蜜|はちみつ} (honey) - in curry, dressings
・{味噌|みそ} (miso) - in soups, stews
・{醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce) - in Western dishes
・{酢|す} (vinegar) - to brighten flavors
・{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう} (milk) - in tomato-based dishes
・インスタントコーヒー (instant coffee) - in chocolate dishes

NUANCE:
The key concept is that the ingredient enhances flavor without being obviously detectable. If you can clearly taste it, it's no longer a {隠|かく}し{味|あじ}.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{隠|かく}す (to hide) + {味|あじ} (flavor) = hidden flavor
